# Phase C error corpus -- runtime / interpreter / property machinery.
# ERRORS.md sections 7-11 (jsrun.c, jsvalue.c, jsproperty.c), rows 132-250.
# Every snippet MUST error in the C build in at least one of flags=0 /
# flags=JS_STRICT. Many of these are strict-only (the loose mode silently
# ignores the violation), which is exactly the difference being compared.
# No try/catch: the bare failing construct is the test.
#
# NOT REACHABLE FROM PURE JS (covered by the in-engine C-API probe tests instead):
#   row 138 "stack underflow!"        -- js_pop past the frame base
#   row 140/141 "stack error!"        -- js_remove / js_replace bad index
#   row 142 "not implemented yet"     -- js_insert is unconditionally an error
#   row 155/156 "not a %s"            -- js_touserdata; no userdata from script
#   rows 180-183 "out of memory"      -- needs js_setlimit(memlimit)
#   row 184 "script ran too long"     -- needs js_setlimit(runlimit)
#   row 178 "endtry: exception stack underflow" -- unbalanced js_endtry
#   row 240 "not an iterator"         -- js_nextiterator on a non-iterator
#   row 215 "array too large" via jsR_setarrayindex -- would need a *flat* array
#           of 2^26 elements (1 GiB) first; the sparse path is taken instead, so
#           only the "length" route (row 220) is testable here.
#   row 222 "cannot create property '%s' on transient object" -- the bytecode
#           SETPROP path leaves `transient` clear, so `'abc'.foo = 1` is a silent
#           no-op in BOTH modes rather than a strict-mode TypeError.
#   row 236 js_delvar non-configurable -- `delete <name>` is already a *compile*
#           error in strict mode (row 306), so the runtime check is unreachable.
#   row 250 js_setlength negative -- Array.prototype.push/pop clamp before the set.
